Capabilities.description:
What the caller may do, decided here rather than in the browser.

The B2B frontend keeps a table mirroring the backend policy and uses it to
decide whether to issue a request at all. Two copies of an authorisation
rule is one too many; this is the served answer.
Capabilities.title: Capabilities

VoiceGrant.description:
What the browser needs to join, and nothing more.

No agent name and no backend label: those are dispatch details the client
has no use for, and b2c currently hands the browser a metadata blob it
simply passes back.
VoiceGrant.title: VoiceGrant

WorkerBootstrap.description:
`{attempt, scenario}` — the only thing a worker is told.

Both halves are passed through as the engine's own documents rather than
re-modelled here: re-describing them would create a second definition of a
contract the engine already owns, free to drift.
WorkerBootstrap.title: WorkerBootstrap

get.description:
A page rather than one result: re-scoring under a new policy adds beside
the old, so a candidate's history stays readable.
The four published exams. Closed set, so no cursor is ever returned.

Expired grants are included with `live` computed, because "your access
ended on the 3rd" is a more useful answer than an empty list.
